content.text: {"label":"system_slowness","explanation":"Payments AHT jumped from about 296 s at 10:00 to 385 s at 10:15 and 556 s at 10:30 (+60% overall, +80% in the last interval). This matches the open P3 incident INC-20261118-1085, opened 10:45: dispute manager / chargeback screens taking 30-60 s to save. Volume was on forecast at 10:15 (-1.9%). The 10:30 jump (+27%) and 27 abandons look like knock-on repeat calls, mainly payment_status_enquiry (1.28x normal), not a new demand driver. No marketing entries are logged. Absences are only slightly above usual (4 vs 2.6 on payments), and staffing is close to plan (38 of 40). General is healthy (95% service level at 10:30, AHT below forecast).","plan_name":"Payments slowness recovery: borrow from general, protect peak, trim repeat contacts","rationale":"Payments is handle-time constrained while the dispute tool is slow, so effective capacity has to be added now and avoidable contacts trimmed until the app team fixes it. General has slack (95% service level, 37 agents on phones). Moving 5 agents is well under the 30% cap and should keep general above 70%. Delaying payments breaks and cancelling payments coaching are free or cheap and cover the late-morning peak. One 2-hour overtime offer to 12 agents (about 5 accept, roughly Rs 3,500) adds capacity from 11:15 within budget. Chat deflection of status-type enquiries at 15% targets the rising payment_status_enquiry repeats plus refund_status at low cost. A waits-over-120 s callback protects abandons during the worst backlog. An outage message is not used because this is not a confirmed customer-facing outage.
